title: FDA Requirements for CYP3A and Transporter Drug Interaction Studies and Labeling in Recent NDA Clinical Pharmacology Reviews
summary: How FDA reviewers assess CYP3A and transporter interactions in recent NDAs: required clinical studies, PBPK acceptance, labeling language, and postmarketing requirements.
body_markdown:
## How FDA evaluates CYP3A and transporter drug interactions in recent NDA clinical pharmacology reviews


FDA clinical pharmacology reviewers follow a consistent sequence for new molecular entities. First, they expect clinical studies with a strong CYP3A index inhibitor and a strong inducer when the drug is a CYP3A substrate. PBPK modeling then extends those results to moderate inhibitors and inducers, but only when reviewers judge the model adequately verified. Perpetrator risk is assessed with midazolam and, where in vitro inhibition exceeds the M12 cutoff for a transporter, with clinical probe-substrate studies. Where the data are incomplete, reviewers fill the gap with labeling (avoid, reduce dose, monitor, or contraindicate) and with postmarketing requirements (PMRs) or commitments (PMCs). The sections below describe the framework reviewers apply and show how it played out across recent original NDAs.


### The framework reviewers apply


**ICH M12 sets the study expectations.** FDA's final *M12 Drug Interaction Studies* guidance (August 2024) recommends that when an investigational drug is a CYP3A substrate, the first clinical DDI studies test a strong index inhibitor and a strong index inducer[443](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=443) . Clarithromycin and itraconazole are listed as strong CYP3A index inhibitors. Carbamazepine, phenytoin and rifampin are listed as strong inducers, and efavirenz as a moderate inducer[444](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=444)[445](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=445) . A negative result with a strong index inhibitor can generally be extrapolated to strong, moderate and weak CYP3A4 inhibitors. Mechanistic modeling can in some cases extrapolate a *positive* finding to moderate and weak inhibitors[448](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=448) . When a drug both inhibits and induces CYP3A, M12 recommends evaluating substrate pharmacokinetics at early and late time points[447](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=447) .


**Transporters follow in vitro cutoffs and clinical follow-up.** M12 recommends in vitro inhibition testing against P-gp, BCRP, OATP1B1/1B3, OAT1/3, OCT2 and MATE1/MATE2-K[418](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=418)[419](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=419) . It sets the following basic cutoffs for ruling out inhibition risk[421](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=421)[422](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=422)[423](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=423)[424](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=424)[425](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=425)[426](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=426) :


Transporter In vitro cutoff to exclude inhibition risk


P-gp/BCRP (oral drug) (dose/250 mL)/IC50 < 10[422](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=422)


P-gp/BCRP (parenteral drug or metabolite) Cmax,u/IC50,u < 0.02[423](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=423)


OATP1B1/1B3 Cmax,inlet,u/IC50,u < 0.1[424](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=424)


OAT1/OAT3/OCT2 Cmax,u/IC50,u < 0.1[425](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=425)


MATE1/MATE2-K Cmax,u/IC50,u < 0.02[426](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=426)


Positive signals may lead to a clinical study, depending on co-medication likelihood and the safety profile of the substrates. Mechanistic static models, PBPK or endogenous biomarkers are acceptable alternatives when their validity is supported[428](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=428) . M12's example clinical substrates are dabigatran etexilate, digoxin and fexofenadine for P-gp[431](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=431) , rosuvastatin and sulfasalazine for BCRP[432](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=432) , statins and bosentan for OATP1B[433](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=433) , furosemide and others for OAT1/3[434](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=434) , and metformin for OCT2/MATE[435](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=435) . FDA notes that no true index substrates exist for transporters[436](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=436) . Plasma coproporphyrin I (CPI) is recognized as an OATP1B1/3 biomarker. A postdose-to-baseline CPI Cmax and AUC ratio below 1.25 indicates low likelihood of a clinical OATP1B DDI[522](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=522)[523](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=523) . Cocktail studies are acceptable when the probes are specific and do not interact with one another[524](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=524) .


**Labeling placement follows the 2024 draft DDI labeling guidance.** The draft *Drug Interaction Information in Human Prescription Drug and Biological Product Labeling* (October 2024) assigns content as follows[194](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=194)[195](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=195) :


- Section 2 carries specific dose modifications for the subject drug[187](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=187) .
- Section 4 lists combinations whose risk clearly outweighs benefit[197](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=197) .
- Section 5 covers clinically significant hazards[198](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=198) .
- Section 7 leads with practical prevention and management instructions[199](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=199)[200](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=200) .
- Section 12.3 holds positive and pertinent negative study results, without management instructions[175](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=175) .


Separately, the 2023 *Clinical Drug Interaction Studies With Combined Oral Contraceptives* guidance expects COC interaction potential to be evaluated and communicated in labeling[525](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=525) . It calls for a COC study for teratogenic drugs even when a CYP3A probe suggests weak or no induction[526](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=526) .


### CYP3A victim interactions: strong inhibitor and inducer studies drive labeling


Across recent reviews, itraconazole and rifampin studies were the standard evidence base. The magnitude of the exposure change mapped fairly predictably to the labeling outcome.


Drug Key clinical finding Labeling or review outcome


Pyrukynd (mitapivat) Itraconazole raised AUC 4.9-fold; rifampin lowered AUC 91%[68](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=68) Avoid strong CYP3A inhibitors and inducers[68](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=68)[42](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=42) . With moderate inhibitors, monitor and cap the dose at 20 mg BID[262](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=262)[248](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=248)


Truqap (capivasertib) Itraconazole raised AUC 1.95-fold; FDA analysis showed efavirenz lowered AUC 60%[81](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=81)[82](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=82) Avoid strong inhibitors and moderate/strong inducers. Reduce to 320 mg BID with moderate inhibitors or an unavoidable strong inhibitor[80](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=80)[48](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=48)


Exkivity (mobocertinib) Itraconazole raised combined molar AUC 6.27-fold; rifampin lowered it about 95%[91](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=91) Avoid strong and moderate inhibitors and inducers. Reduce the dose about 50% with ECG monitoring if a moderate inhibitor is unavoidable[91](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=91)[94](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=94)[54](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=54)


Ibtrozi (taletrectinib) Itraconazole raised AUC 3.3-fold; rifampin lowered AUC 86%[85](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=85) Avoid strong and moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors and inducers[87](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=87)[52](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=52)


Ogsiveo (nirogacestat) Itraconazole raised single-dose AUC 8.2-fold[98](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=98) FDA revised labeling to avoid strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors and inducers[103](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=103)[104](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=104)[56](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=56)


Beqalzi (sonrotoclax) Posaconazole raised AUC up to 16-fold; itraconazole 11-fold[109](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=109) 20 mg daily target with strong inhibitors, which are avoided during ramp-up. Avoid strong or moderate inducers[110](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=110)[111](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=111)[58](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=58)


Zenbexus (iberdomide) Itraconazole raised AUC about 2.4-fold[75](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=75) Avoid strong inhibitors or reduce the dose. Lower starting dose with moderate inhibitors[78](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=78)[77](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=77)[45](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=45)


Jascayd (nerandomilast) Itraconazole raised AUC 2.2-fold[64](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=64) Halve the dose (18 to 9 mg BID) with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Avoid moderate or strong inducers[61](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=61)[66](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=66)[41](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=41)


Joenja (leniolisib) Itraconazole raised AUC about 2-fold; quinidine had no effect[89](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=89) Avoid strong CYP3A inhibitors. No adjustment for P-gp or weak/moderate inhibitors[89](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=89)[53](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=53)


Journavx (suzetrigine) Itraconazole raised AUC 4.79-fold; rifampin lowered AUC 93%[352](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=352)[353](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=353) Strong inhibitors contraindicated. Reduce the dose with moderate inhibitors. Avoid strong or moderate inducers[353](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=353)[355](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=355)[334](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=334)


Litfulo (ritlecitinib) Rifampin lowered AUC about 44%[263](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=263) Avoid strong CYP3A inducers because of potential loss of efficacy[264](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=264)[244](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=244)


Lazcluze (lazertinib) Rifampin lowered AUC to 16% of control[258](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=258) Review recommended avoiding moderate CYP3A4 inducers as well[259](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=259)[242](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=242)


Oxbryta (voxelotor) Itraconazole raised exposure only about 10%[70](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=70) No inhibitor adjustment. Higher doses specified for unavoidable strong or moderate inducers[70](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=70)[43](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=43)


Exkivity, Truseltiq, Ukoniq and Oxbryta have since been withdrawn from the US market; their rows show how reviewers handled the interaction data at approval, not current labeling.


Two patterns stand out. First, contraindications are reserved for the largest effects or for combinations with serious safety consequences. Exxua carries a contraindication for strong CYP3A4 inhibitors, which raise its exposure about 5-fold, and a dose reduction for moderate inhibitors (about 2.6-fold)[509](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=509) . Myqorzo (aficamten) contraindicates rifampin; PBPK predicted a 79% AUC decrease[253](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=253)[254](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=254)[237](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=237) . Second, induction findings are interpreted mechanistically. For Vanrafia (atrasentan), rifampin's concurrent OATP1B inhibition masked CYP3A induction, so AUC was unchanged even though trough concentrations fell by more than 80%. Reviewers still supported avoiding strong or moderate inducers[265](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=265)[266](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=266)[247](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=247) . For Brenzavvy (bexagliflozin), the reviewer cautioned that a three-day rifampin pretreatment might not capture maximal induction[267](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=267)[249](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=249) .


### PBPK for moderate inhibitors and inducers: accepted only when verified


Reviewers routinely accept PBPK to extrapolate clinical strong-perpetrator results to moderate perpetrators. Accepted examples include:


- Mobocertinib: about 2-fold AUC with moderate inhibitors and about 60% lower exposure with efavirenz[91](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=91)[93](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=93)
- Taletrectinib: up to 2.6-fold AUC with moderate inhibitors[86](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=86)
- Suzetrigine: 3.0-fold AUC with fluconazole, which supported a reduced regimen[251](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=251)
- Rilzabrutinib: about 70% lower AUC with efavirenz[255](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=255)
- Lazertinib: at least 44% lower AUC with efavirenz[258](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=258)[245](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=245)


Reviewers also reject or limit models that are not adequately verified:


- **Sohonos (palovarotene):** the model was not considered adequate for predicting most CYP inhibitor or inducer effects[291](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=291)[274](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=274) .
- **Quviviq (daridorexant):** the model was verified against diltiazem and efavirenz but could not accurately predict the magnitude of strong-modulator effects[297](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=297)[277](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=277) .
- **Wayrilz (rilzabrutinib):** the victim model's efavirenz extrapolation was accepted (above), but the reviewer found the cimetidine and dexamethasone perpetrator models inadequately verified[348](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=348)[349](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=349)[325](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=325) . Transporter-substrate predictions were considered inadequate[321](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=321)[288](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=288) .
- **Filspari (sparsentan) and Truqap:** reviewers flagged that rifampin models omitting P-gp (and, for capivasertib, UGT2B7) induction may underpredict the decrease in exposure[299](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=299)[285](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=285)[272](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=272)[252](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=252) .


When modeling cannot resolve the question, FDA converts the gap into a PMR. Examples:


- Truseltiq (infigratinib): itraconazole raised exposure sevenfold, but the moderate-inhibitor effect was uncertain, so FDA required a moderate-inhibitor study[165](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=165)[166](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=166)[135](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=135) .
- Vonjo (pacritinib): FDA required a revised, validated PBPK analysis, with a clinical study as backup if results are inconclusive[149](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=149)[119](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=119) .
- Jideytro (zidesamtinib): nonlinear PK made moderate-inhibitor effects unclear. FDA proposed excluding moderate CYP3A inhibitors in labeling and a PMR allowing either a clinical trial or PBPK[140](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=140)[142](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=142)[115](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=115) .


### CYP3A perpetrator effects: midazolam, induction and contraceptives


Midazolam remains the standard probe for perpetrator assessment. Labeling scales with the observed effect:


Drug Effect on CYP3A substrates Labeling or review outcome


Paxlovid (nirmatrelvir/ritonavir) Midazolam AUC ratio 14.3[496](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=496) Oral midazolam contraindicated, along with other CYP3A-dependent drugs[496](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=496)[495](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=495)[459](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=459)


Sunlenca (lenacapavir) Midazolam AUC increased 3.59-fold[402](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=402) Avoid CYP3A substrates for which small concentration changes may cause serious toxicity[404](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=404)[388](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=388)


Scemblix (asciminib) Midazolam AUC ratio 1.36 at 40 mg BID; 88% increase predicted at 200 mg BID[357](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=357)[358](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=358) Monitor at 80 mg/day. At 200 mg BID, avoid narrow-margin substrates or reduce their dose[357](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=357)[327](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=327)


Rhapsido (remibrutinib) PBPK predicted about a 20% to 25% AUC increase at the 25 mg BID dose[373](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=373) Sensitive CYP3A substrates and the evaluated COCs may be coadministered[374](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=374)[333](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=333)


Journavx (suzetrigine), inducer Midazolam AUC lowered about 48%[350](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=350) Avoid CYP3A substrates for which small concentration changes could cause loss of efficacy[354](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=354)[334](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=334)


Pyrukynd (mitapivat), inducer Midazolam AUC lowered 21% to 57% across doses[365](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=365) Monitor narrow-therapeutic-index CYP3A substrates. Advise nonhormonal or additional barrier contraception[367](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=367)[508](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=508)


Induction is the area where reviewers most often treat sponsor predictions with skepticism:


- **Voranigo (vorasidenib):** the sponsor's PBPK predicted an 80% or greater decrease in midazolam AUC. FDA considered that estimate potentially excessive, classed vorasidenib as a possible weak-to-moderate inducer, and identified a postmarketing study to determine the magnitude[361](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=361)[328](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=328) .
- **Itovebi (inavolisib):** FDA could not rule out induction from PBPK[339](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=339)[340](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=340)[335](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=335) and obtained a PMC for a clinical study with a sensitive CYP3A substrate[137](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=137)[112](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=112) .
- **Joenja (leniolisib):** the induction model could not predict the magnitude of the effect, so FDA required a cocktail DDI study that includes midazolam[38](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=38)[39](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=39)[31](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=31) .


Negative midazolam studies have resolved in vitro signals:


- Vanrafia showed in vitro time-dependent inhibition and induction, but midazolam AUC and Cmax ratios were 1.10 and 1.09[369](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=369)[332](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=332) .
- Bylvay showed an in vitro intestinal CYP3A inhibition signal, but no inhibition in vivo[466](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=466)[450](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=450) .


### Transporter interactions: probe-substrate studies and biomarkers


**P-gp.** Digoxin and dabigatran studies drove monitoring language rather than contraindications:


- Xolremdi (mavorixafor) raised digoxin AUC 1.65-fold. The review recommended monitoring narrow-margin P-gp substrates and serum digoxin concentrations[32](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=32)[18](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=18) .
- Cibinqo (abrocitinib) raised dabigatran AUC 1.53-fold. No dabigatran adjustment was required, but monitoring or titration was recommended for sensitive P-gp substrates[399](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=399)[381](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=381) .
- Paxlovid raised dabigatran AUC 1.94-fold. Labeling recommends dose reduction or avoidance depending on indication and renal function[496](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=496)[459](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=459) .


**BCRP and OATP1B.** Rosuvastatin is the workhorse probe:


- Rezdiffra (resmetirom) raised rosuvastatin AUC 1.8-fold and also increased exposure to other statins. FDA set statin dose caps: simvastatin and rosuvastatin 20 mg/day, atorvastatin and pravastatin 40 mg/day[222](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=222)[223](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=223)[210](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=210) .
- Hernexeos (zongertinib) raised rosuvastatin AUC 2.30-fold. Coadministration with sensitive BCRP substrates is not recommended. CPI data argued against relevant OATP1B inhibition, so no adjustment is needed for OATP1B substrates[33](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=33)[34](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=34)[27](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=27) .
- Rhapsido raised rosuvastatin AUC 1.65-fold, and labeling recommends monitoring with narrow-margin BCRP substrates[229](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=229)[230](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=230)[212](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=212) . Its unchanged CPI supported no OATP1B1 inhibition[476](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=476)[453](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=453) .
- Fabhalta (iptacopan) had no significant effect on digoxin or rosuvastatin. P-gp, BCRP and OATP1B substrates may be coadministered[234](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=234)[235](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=235)[218](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=218) .


**Renal transporters.**


- Cosela (trilaciclib) raised metformin AUC 1.65-fold and cut its renal clearance 37%. FDA found no dose modification warranted because trilaciclib is dosed intermittently[35](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=35)[36](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=36)[28](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=28) .
- Vafseo (vadadustat) roughly doubled furosemide exposure through probable OAT3 inhibition. Reviewers added that labeling should note the potential need for dose adjustment[395](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=395)[397](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=397)[380](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=380) .
- Blujepa (gepotidacin) showed no MATE1/2-K interaction with cimetidine[96](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=96)[55](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=55) .


**Transporter PMRs are common** when in vitro signals exceed cutoffs and no clinical data exist:


- Rezurock (belumosudil): clinical study of sensitive P-gp/BCRP/OATP1B1 substrates[159](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=159)[126](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=126)
- Jideytro: required P-gp/BCRP substrate trial[142](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=142)[143](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=143)[115](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=115)
- Augtyro (repotrectinib): transporter-substrate trials[147](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=147)[118](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=118)
- Ibtrozi: clinical study of sensitive CYP3A and transporter substrates[160](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=160)[127](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=127)
- Avmapki Fakzynja: MATE2-K substrate or endogenous biomarker evaluation[156](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=156)[123](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=123)
- Joenja: cocktail study with rosuvastatin and metformin[40](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=40)[31](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=31)
- Lupkynis (voclosporin): PMC for an OATP1B1 substrate study[158](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=158)[125](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=125)
- Ojemda (tovorafenib): interim labeling to avoid sensitive CYP3A substrates and hormonal contraceptives, with PMRs for enzyme and BCRP substrate studies[138](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=138)[113](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=113)


### Postmarketing requirements and commitments as a bridging tool


Recent approvals show FDA accepting an approval with DDI gaps when labeling provides interim protection. In those cases FDA obtains a PMR or PMC to generate the missing data:


- Inducer studies: Jascayd (moderate and strong)[144](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=144)[116](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=116) , Hernexeos (moderate)[164](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=164)[131](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=131) , Ensacove (strong)[157](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=157)[130](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=130) , Ukoniq (strong)[161](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=161)[134](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=134) , and Vanflyta (weak, with the active metabolite)[167](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=167)[136](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=136)
- Bidirectional CYP3A studies: Rezlidhia[139](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=139)[114](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=114)
- Combined CYP3A/P-gp questions: Tepmetko received an itraconazole PMR and a rifampin PMC. Interim labeling avoids strong CYP3A4 inducers and dual strong CYP3A/P-gp inhibitors[151](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=151)[152](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=152)[153](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=153)[120](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=120)


### Practical implications for sponsors


- Plan itraconazole (or clarithromycin) and rifampin studies early. Reviewers expect these clinical anchors, and labeling recommendations for strong perpetrators rarely rest on modeling alone[443](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=443)[444](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=444) .
- Verify PBPK models against clinical moderate-perpetrator data where possible. Account for P-gp and UGT induction by rifampin. Unverified models lead to PMRs or conservative avoidance language[297](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=297)[299](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=299)[149](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=149) .
- For perpetrator risk, characterize induction clinically. Reviewers discount PBPK-only induction predictions and may require clinical substrate studies after approval[361](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=361)[339](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=339)[38](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=38) .
- Use CPI and cocktail designs to resolve OATP1B and multi-transporter signals efficiently. FDA has accepted CPI data to remove OATP1B labeling concerns[523](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=523)[33](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=33)[476](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=476) .
- Address hormonal contraceptives explicitly for CYP3A inducers, consistent with the 2023 COC guidance[525](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=525)[367](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=367) .
- Draft Sections 2, 4, 5, 7 and 12.3 consistently with the 2024 draft DDI labeling guidance. Put management instructions in Section 7 and study data in Section 12.3[199](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=199)[175](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-cyp3a-and-transporter-drug?showSourceNumber=175) .
